subject: How to hide diagonal line in legend when using both color and fill

messages.author: 75db403eb2b8ba68
messages.subject: How to hide diagonal line in legend when using both color and fill
parts:
Hi there, when using both color and fill on e.g. a bagchart, I cant get rid of the "color" diagonal line in the legend key - even though I place , eg. color="black" outside of aes.Any idas as to what I am doing wrong?

Thanks:

example: 
library(ggplot2)
y <- rnorm(10)
x <- letters[1:10]
z<- sample(letters[11:14], 10, replace=T)
test <- data.frame(cbind(x,y,z))

ggplot(test, aes(x=x, y=y,fill=z))+facet_grid(.~z, scales="free")+geom_bar(color="black")

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: How to hide diagonal line in legend when using both color and fill
parts:
Hi Andreas,
as I said to Felipe just 10 hours ago. There's no option to do this, but there's a workaround. Plot the geom_bar two times, one for the legend without the black line and then with the black line but the legend off.

ggplot(test, aes(x=x, y=y,fill=z))+facet_grid(.~z, scales="free")+ geom_bar () +  geom_bar(color="black", legend = FALSE) 

HTH

Luciano

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: How to hide diagonal line in legend when using both color and fill
parts: Hi:

On Sat, Nov 16, 2013 at 6:15 AM, Adrian Quevedo <adrian...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello, it seems that legend=FALSE is deprecated,
> I tried to plot to times without this,
> the diagonal line is hide but I lose two lines of the four around each key,
> and around each bar,
> is there something new for this ?
> thanks

The legend = FALSE argument has more or less been deprecated since
version 0.9.0. Usually it can be replaced by guide = "none" inside the
scale_*() functions, but that won't work in this case. One way out is
to set a color aesthetic inside an aes() statement in geom_bar() and
use scale_color_identity(). This will put a black border around the
bars but not around the legend keys, since scale_identity() does not
produce a legend by default. To compensate, you can use the theming
system to put black borders on the legend keys.

I grabbed the data from the original message and modified the data
fra. Let's look at your original chart:

library(ggplot2)
y <- rnorm(10)
x <- letters[1:10]

z <- sample(letters[11:14], 10, replace=TRUE)
test1 <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, z = z)


# Since you have defined y, you need to use stat = "identity" in geom_bar()
# to get rid of the litany of warnings:
ggplot(test1, aes(x=x, y=y,fill=z)) +
facet_grid(. ~ z, scales="free") +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", color="black")


You'll get warnings about stacking not being well-defined when ymin =
0, but they can be ignored. If this is the way you want your graph to
look except for the borders, then the following should finish it:

ggplot(test1, aes(x=x, y=y,fill=z)) +
facet_grid(. ~ z, scales="free") +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", aes(color = "black")) +
scale_color_identity() +
theme(legend.key = element_rect(colour = "black", size = 1))

If you want the look in the original post, substitute y = abs(y) for y
= y in the ggplot() call. The trick is to map a single color in
geom_bar() and then use the identity scale on it; by default,
scale_identity() does not produce a legend guide. This part will put
borders around the bars but not the legend keys. That's where the last
line comes in: we use the theming system to put a black border around
each key item and increase the default size so that they will be
visible. If you find them too thick, reduce the value of size in the
last line.

HTH,
Dennis
